title: RobotsMali AI4D Lab / Laboratoire IAPD RobotsMali
description: Responsible artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to accelerate the transformation of Francophone countries in the Sahel region, but research and innovation capacity in this region is very weak compared to Anglophone African countries. Among the many challenges research institutions confront in the region is the basic one of language. Knowledge of English among students is very rare and constitutes a formidable barrier to developing competence in AI.  The RobotsMali AI4D Lab seeks to build capacity within both public and private sectors to conduct local, relevant and multidisciplinary research aimed at contributing to the social and economic development of the region. The lab is a collaborative research hub and nexus of the major public universities of Mali, private universities, government, social organizations and industry. The lab will support multidisciplinary teams to research interventions that can improve educational outcomes and literacy, contribute to the enhancement of AI teaching and research capabilities in Francophone institutions of higher learning, and incubate AI-powered startups. The activities of the lab will revolve around the pillars of community-building and skill development, scientific rigour, commitment to ethical and responsible practices, gender equality and inclusion.  This project is a part of the Artificial Intelligence for Development (AI4D) program, a five-year partnership between IDRC and the United Kingdom's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office to support policy, innovations and expanded leadership to spur safe and responsible AI development in Africa. The vision of the new partnership is to support an inclusive, responsible AI ecosystem that improves quality of life for all in Africa and beyond. / L'intelligence artificielle responsable (IA) a le potentiel d'accélérer la transformation des pays francophones de la région du Sahel, mais les capacités de recherche et d'innovation dans cette région sont très faibles par rapport aux pays africains anglophones. Parmi les nombreux défis auxquels les institutions de recherche sont confrontées dans la région, il y a celui, fondamental, de la langue. La connaissance de l'anglais chez les étudiants est très rare et constitue un obstacle formidable au développement de compétences en IA. Le laboratoire IAPD RobotsMali vise à renforcer les capacités des secteurs public et privé à mener des recherches locales, pertinentes et multidisciplinaires afin de contribuer au développement social et économique de la région. Le laboratoire est un centre de recherche collaborative et un lien entre les principales universités publiques du Mali, les universités privées, le gouvernement, les organisations sociales et l'industrie. Le laboratoire soutiendra des équipes pluridisciplinaires dans la recherche d'interventions susceptibles d'améliorer les résultats scolaires et l'alphabétisation, de contribuer à l'amélioration des capacités d'enseignement et de recherche en matière d'IA dans les établissements d'enseignement supérieur francophones, et d'incuber des jeunes entreprises alimentées par l'IA. Les activités du laboratoire s'articuleront autour des piliers suivants : renforcement de la collectivité et développement des compétences, rigueur scientifique, engagement en faveur de pratiques éthiques et responsables, égalité des genres et inclusion. Ce projet s'inscrit dans le cadre du programme d'intelligence artificielle pour le développement (IAPD), un partenariat de cinq ans entre le CRDI et le Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office du Royaume-Uni visant à soutenir les politiques, les innovations et un leadership élargi afin de stimuler le développement sûr et responsable de l'IA en Afrique. scope_basis: Contribution co-funds the national population census.
title: Mali RGPH5 census — special review, Swedish contribution
description:
The Malian general census takes place every 10 years. The fifth census was planned to take place 2016-2021 with 2019 being the year when most of the work will be implemented. The process was delayed and concluded 2022. The census is a large and complicated project in a vast country like Mali that has limited infrastructure and security challenges. The census will produce data that will be used for social and economic development in the country and to follow up on development interventions.

The Swedish contribution will be used by the Malian government to co-fund the fifth population census (RGPH5) in Mali. By Malian law and according to UN recommendations these are to take place every 10 years. The census is not a sample but a complete inventory of people and their accommodation in Mali. The census will provide data and analyses on: 1) total number of inhabitants in Mali and structure by sex and age 2) spatial distribution of people according to administrative unites and type of residence 3) social, economic and cultural characteristics of the Malian population 4) level, structure and tendencies regarding fertility, civil status, mortality and migration 5) indicators for lobbying regarding vulnerable groups, especially old people, women, young people, people living with handicaps, displaced people, orphans etc 6) conclusions regarding the evolution of the data above since the 1976 census 7) projections and demographic prospects into the future 8) characteristics of households, habitat and livelihoods 9) analysis and cartography of poverty 10) updated statistics on villages, wells and other collective social infrastructure 11) geo-referenced information on collective social infrastructure and economic units 12) establishment of demographic indicators 13) capacity building on data collection, analysis and communication using modern information technology The intervention produces baseline information and analyses that are crucial to the design of development action,

title: Strengthening the use of open data in Francophone Africa to improve policy and citizen engagement and drive innovation
description: Despite the positive potential and relative progress of open data for development, there are still gaps in creating and sharing high quality, timely, relevant, and accessible data in developing countries. Past research on Francophone Africa has highlighted the lack of capacity among data producers, particularly governments, to release high quality, timely data about public issues. Many countries still lack foundational legislation, such as right-to-information laws, or a lack of political will to enforce them. There are also concerns about data sharing, power, and privacy. Further, in many cases there is a lack of capacity amongst actors in understanding the potential of sharing data or technical practices in releasing digital open data. Another major challenge is a lack of resources to address capacity and skills gaps, as many resources are not available in French and local languages. These capacity challenges have a negative effect on the release of quality open data about government services such as justice, government budgets and spending, agriculture, education, and more. These challenges contribute to a resulting lack of use of open data, despite demand from a range of stakeholders. Nevertheless, where data is available, useful innovations are emerging, such as mapping aid data to increase the efficiency of service delivery. scope_basis: Contribution to a population and housing census.
title: Mali fifth general population and housing census (RGPH5) — Swedish contribution
description:
The Malian general census takes place every 10 years. The fifth census was planned to take place 2016-2021 with 2019 being the year when most of the work will be implemented. The process was delayed and concluded 2022. The census is a large and complicated project in a vast country like Mali that has limited infrastructure and security challenges. The census will produce data that will be used for social and economic development in the country and to follow up on development interventions.

The Swedish contribution will be used by the Malian government to co-fund the fifth population census (RGPH5) in Mali. By Malian law and according to UN recommendations these are to take place every 10 years. The census is not a sample but a complete inventory of people and their accommodation in Mali. The census will provide data and analyses on: 1) total number of inhabitants in Mali and structure by sex and age 2) spatial distribution of people according to administrative unites and type of residence 3) social, economic and cultural characteristics of the Malian population 4) level, structure and tendencies regarding fertility, civil status, mortality and migration 5) indicators for lobbying regarding vulnerable groups, especially old people, women, young people, people living with handicaps, displaced people, orphans etc 6) conclusions regarding the evolution of the data above since the 1976 census 7) projections and demographic prospects into the future 8) characteristics of households, habitat and livelihoods 9) analysis and cartography of poverty 10) updated statistics on villages, wells and other collective social infrastructure 11) geo-referenced information on collective social infrastructure and economic units 12) establishment of demographic indicators 13) capacity building on data collection, analysis and communication using modern information technology The intervention produces baseline information and analyses that are crucial to the design of development action,

title: China Eximbank provides RMB 1.134 billion government concessional loan for Mali Digital 2020 Project
description: On September 28, 2018, the Government of Mali and China Eximbank signed an RMB 1.134 billion (XOF 93,790,872,000) government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Mali Digital 2020 Project. The borrowing terms of the GCL are unknown. However, it is known that the proceeds of the GCL were to be used by the borrower to finance a commercial contract between the Government of Mali and China International Telecommunications Construction Corporation (CITCC).  The purpose of the project is to lay 817.4 km of intercity fiber optic cable, install twelve OSN 3500 type terminals, install a a GPON (Gigabit Passive Optical Network) urban network with 100 km of fiber optic cable, and install about 50 GPON terminals to interconnect the government institutions. More specifically, the project involves laying fiber optic cables to connecting the cities of Kidal, Gao and Timbuktu to the city of Mopti; laying fiber optic cable along the Gao-Ansongo-Labbezanga-Nigerian border route; laying fiber optic cable along the Kidal-Algerian border route; laying fiber optic cable along the Bamako-Kourémalé-Guinean border route; laying fiber optic cable along the Sevaré – Koro-Burkina Faso border route; establishing a surveillance network made up of 200 cameras and 50 LTE sites; establishing an internal secure communications network for the government; and establishing an electronic identification card system.   CITCC is the contractor responsible for project implementation. In February 2019, Ambassador Zhu Liying visited the construction site and had a discussion with the head of the project team. It is unclear if the project is on track for its 2020 completion date.
